builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SpecEngineeringBench: Evaluating Coding Agents as Autonomous Specification Engineers
summary: It replaces ad hoc evaluation of coding agents on cued test-generation tasks (issue descriptions, designated test entry points) with an uncued benchmark of 100 instances across 78 Python repositories measuring defect discovery and fault localization. Cost is limited to agent API calls and harness setup for test execution, coverage, and localization scoring, with no training or cluster requirement. It can fail as a selection signal if teams read pass rate or coverage as evidence of defect-finding ability, since the paper shows these metrics decouple and function-level localization remains near 51%.
rationale: The benchmark is directly usable through API-based agents at modest cost, and its central finding warns that high test validity and coverage do not imply real defect discovery, which changes how the reader should validate coding agents in production.
technique: Uncued benchmark for autonomous specification engineering

claims.statement: It replaces ad hoc evaluation of coding agents on cued test-generation tasks (issue descriptions, designated test entry points) with an uncued benchmark of 100 instances across 78 Python repositories measuring defect discovery and fault localization. Cost is limited to agent API calls and harness setup for test execution, coverage, and localization scoring, with no training or cluster requirement. It can fail as a selection signal if teams read pass rate or coverage as evidence of defect-finding ability, since the paper shows these metrics decouple and function-level localization remains near 51%.

Across seven frontier coding agents: 91.47% Head Pass Rate and 80.48% change-focused coverage but only 26.36% fail-to-pass rate; localization recall falls from 78.11% (file) to 51.29% (function); autonomous test generation improves file/function/hunk localization recall by 4.99/2.77/2.69 points over reusing existing repository tests.
